question.text: Per the current NISM V-A workbook, for purchases/switch-ins in mutual fund schemes other than liquid/overnight schemes (effective from February 1, 2021), what condition determines applicability of the purchase NAV irrespective of application size and time of receipt?

answer.text: The investor must submit additional KYC documents
The transaction must be approved by the fund manager
The funds must be available/credited to the scheme's bank account before the cut-off time
The investor must provide a declaration of source of funds

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM V-A workbook footnote states that from February 1, 2021, for schemes other than liquid/overnight, the applicable purchase/switch-in NAV depends on when funds are available for utilisation, irrespective of application size and time of receipt. The earlier Rs. 2 lakh threshold no longer applies. The Trap: The older "Rs. 2 lakh and above only" framing is no longer the rule — the funds-available-before-cut-off condition applies generally for non-liquid/non-overnight schemes. Cross-Exam Context: NISM V-A and II-B both test cut-off-time/funds-available NAV applicability in detail; the liquid/overnight schemes follow a distinct treatment.
